# `entire why` Design

## Goal

Introduce a prototype command named `entire why` that helps users understand why the current `HEAD` version of a file looks the way it does.

The command should feel like a blame-oriented history browser:

- First view: a blame-derived full-file view of the current file
- Second view: checkpoint detail for the selected blamed line's owning blame block when Entire metadata exists
- Third view: session detail within that checkpoint
- Optional no-arg interactive entry: a file browser rooted at the current working directory that lets the user choose a file before entering the why view

For commits that are not linked to Entire metadata, the command should still be useful by falling back to generic Git commit detail and a file-scoped diff.

## Prototype Scope

The prototype is intentionally narrow.

Included:

- Command name: `entire why`
- Input shape:
  - `entire why <path>`
  - `entire why -L <line> <path>`
  - `entire why --lines <start-end> <path>`
  - `entire why` in an interactive shell should open a file browser rooted at `pwd`
- Explicit mode controls:
  - `-i` / `--interactive` to force the TUI path
  - `--no-pager` to disable pager use for static output
- Local-only metadata resolution
- `HEAD`-only blame view
- Commit-first provenance model
- Non-interactive text output
- Interactive TUI when a real interactive shell is available
- Checkpoint-first detail navigation
- Summary text with fallback when no generated summary exists
- Syntax highlighting in the TUI code pane

Explicitly out of scope for the prototype:

- Remote checkpoint fetching
- Arbitrary revisions such as `entire why <rev> -- <path>`
- Automatic summary generation during `entire why`
- JSON output
- Rename/copy-following flags such as `-M` and `-C`
- Uncommitted working tree attribution

## Product Decisions

### Provenance Model

The first screen is commit-first, not checkpoint-first.

`git blame` remains the source of truth for line provenance. Entire metadata enriches blamed commits by default when available, and that enrichment is part of the main value of `entire why`, not a secondary or hidden detail.

This is important because existing checkpoint/session storage is not sufficient to reconstruct exact current-line ownership without effectively reimplementing blame semantics.

### History Coverage

The first screen should show the file itself in order from top to bottom, not a reduced list of blocks.

Every source line in the current `HEAD` version of the file should remain visible in both static and interactive modes. Entire metadata should enrich those lines, not replace the file view with a block browser.

Rows whose owning blame block has Entire metadata should be visually emphasized. Rows without Entire metadata should remain visible with blank or placeholder Entire fields.

### Detail Hierarchy

Pressing `enter` or space on a selected blamed line should open a checkpoint-first detail screen when that line's owning blamed block has an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.

If no checkpoint exists for the blamed commit, detail falls back to generic Git commit information plus a file-scoped diff for the selected file.

### Summary Policy

The first screen should show:

- Saved generated summary text when present
- Otherwise a fallback summary derived from existing local metadata, such as checkpoint intent or commit subject

`entire why` should not generate summaries on demand in the prototype.

## User Experience

### First View

The first view should resemble an Entire-enriched blame browser rather than a plain blame dump or a generic table.

Conceptually it has one primary surface:

- A full-file code view with a metadata gutter beside each source line

The file itself is the thing being browsed. Blame blocks remain important, but only as the provenance unit behind each line and as the target for detail drill-down.

The first view must do more than restate normal Git blame information. When Entire metadata is available for the blamed commit, that Entire context should be visible in the main screen by default so users can immediately understand not just who last touched the code, but also whether the change came through an Entire checkpoint and which agent or session context was involved.

The intended layout is:

- Left side or metadata gutter: blame-oriented identity fields such as short commit hash, author, checkpoint ID, agent, and line number
- Right side or code pane: the source line itself

In other words, the Entire-specific fields belong in the default scanning surface of the first screen, not only in an expanded detail view.

Each visible file row should expose:

- File line number
- Short commit hash
- Author
- Checkpoint ID, when present
- Agent name, when present
- The source line itself

For Entire-linked lines, the main screen should aim to surface these fields directly in the primary browsing experience:

- Entire checkpoint ID
- AI agent used
- Short AI-generated summary, when already a…146 chars truncated…n "blame with a separate details screen."

For non-Entire commits, those same metadata slots may be blank, replaced with placeholders, or omitted in a visually consistent way, but the layout should still preserve the same overall scanning model.

Because summary text is often too wide to show next to every line without destroying file readability, the interactive view may surface summary in selected-line metadata rather than in every row of the gutter.

### Non-Interactive Mode

Non-interactive mode should be the baseline behavior.

It should:

- Produce a readable text rendering of the file line-by-line
- Work when stdout is piped
- Work in accessibility mode
- Preserve compatibility with pager-based presentation such as `less` or `delta`
- Support line-restricted views via `--lines` / `-L`

If output is long, the command should use the same pager strategy already used by `entire explain`.

For non-interactive output, pager-based syntax highlighting remains acceptable and desirable. Users who already route CLI output through tools such as `delta` should be able to benefit from that setup.

The current command contract is intentionally split:

- interactive terminal without overrides: default to the TUI
- non-interactive, piped, or accessibility mode: default to static output
- `--interactive`: force the TUI and fail clearly if a real interactive terminal is unavailable
- `--no-pager`: keep static output but bypass pager integration

In implementation terms, the TUI path should require all of the following:

- accessibility mode is not enabled
- output is attached to a terminal-capable writer
- interactive prompting is possible under the CLI's normal `CanPromptInteractively()` rules

### Interactive Mode

When a real interactive shell is available, the command should offer a TUI.

The TUI should reuse established Bubble Tea interaction patterns already used elsewhere in the CLI:

- Optional file-browser mode when `entire why` is invoked without a path
- Browse mode for the full file
- Detail mode for checkpoint or commit detail
- Session detail mode
- Viewport scrolling for long content
- `j` and `k`, plus arrow keys, for movement
- `enter` or space to open detail
- `esc` or `q` to go back

The visible help text should prioritize accessible/default controls:

- arrow keys
- `enter`
- `esc`

Vim-style aliases should still exist, but they do not need to be shown in help text. The intended hidden alias policy is:

- `h` = back
- `j` = down
- `k` = up
- `l` = open / drill down / confirm

This means the documented controls remain accessibility-first while users familiar with vim-like navigation can still rely on the same directional vocabulary across views.

The TUI should include syntax highlighting in the code pane for the prototype.

The recommended approach is to use a pure-Go highlighter that emits ANSI-colored terminal text for direct rendering inside Bubble Tea viewports. The leading candidate is Chroma because it is pure Go, supports many languages, and can format to terminal color output. Markdown-focused renderers such as Glamour are less suitable as the primary engine because this screen is fundamentally a source-code browser, not a markdown document renderer.

Syntax highlighting should be applied only to the code pane, not to the metadata gutter. The metadata side should remain styled via Lip Gloss so the two layers remain visually distinct.

In the interactive view, the selected line may also drive a compact metadata header showing richer fields such as date and summary, while the scrollable body stays focused on the file itself.

The interactive view should favor code readability over stuffing every Entire field into the per-line gutter. The settled layout direction is:

- A compact left gutter for the file view with commit hash, author, checkpoint ID, and line number
- A richer top metadata bar for the currently selected line, using labeled fields such as commit, author, date, checkpoint, agent, and summary
- Detail screens that use clearly separated sections instead of one continuous text wall

General pager-style shortcuts should be supported in all TUI views:

- `g` jumps to the top
- `G` jumps to the bottom

Checkpoint detail should use explicit focusable panes rather than treating the entire screen as one undifferentiated scroll surface. The current pane model is:

- `Sessions`
- `Generated Checkpoint Summary`
- `File Diff`

`tab` cycles forward through those panes when more than one is present. The focused pane should:

- receive the active bordered-panel treatment
- own `j` / `k` or arrow-key scrolling when it is a scrollable pane
- expand to show materially more content than the unfocused panes

Unfocused panes may render as previews rather than full sections. In particular:

- the session list may show only the first few rows plus a “more sessions” hint
- the generated summary may show only an initial preview when unfocused
- the diff may show only an initial preview when unfocused

### Interactive Entry Without a Path

If `entire why` is invoked with no path in an interactive shell, it should start in a lightweight file browser rooted at the current working directory.

This browser should:

- Show all files and directories, including dotfiles
- Sort directories before files
- Allow directory traversal with `j`/`k`, arrows, `enter`, and `h` or `backspace`
- Preserve browser directory and cursor position when the user opens a file and later returns from the why view

If `entire why` is invoked with no path in a non-interactive environment, it should return an error rather than attempting to print a directory listing.

If `--interactive` is supplied explicitly, the same rule should apply: failure is preferable to silently falling back to static output.

## Data Flow

The command should follow this pipeline:

1. Validate that the target path exists at `HEAD`
2. If `--lines` / `-L` is present, parse numeric-only input:
   - `N`
   - `start-end`
   Both `-L` and `--lines` should accept either form.
3. Run `git blame --line-porcelain -- <path>` against `HEAD`
   - when a line range is present, pass it through as `git blame -L <git-range>`
3. Parse blame output into line records
4. Collapse adjacent lines with the same blamed commit into contiguous blame blocks
5. For each unique blamed commit:
   - Resolve the local commit object
   - Parse `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer if present
   - If linked, read checkpoint summary and latest relevant session metadata from local checkpoint storage
   - If the blamed commit object is missing locally, or checkpoint/session metadata is partially unavailable, degrade to plain blame metadata for the affected lines instead of aborting the whole overview
6. Flatten blame blocks into a full-file row model that preserves the owning block for each source line
7. Detect or derive the file language for syntax highlighting, preferably from the target filename and falling back safely when unknown
8. Render syntax-highlighted code lines for the code pane in interactive mode
9. Render either:
   - a static text blame-like file view, or
   - an interactive Bubble Tea model backed by the same row data
10. In the no-arg interactive case, resolve the target path through a TUI file browser before loading blame data

The key invariants are:

- Git determines which commit last touched the current line
- Entire determines what extra context should be surfaced alongside that commit in the first view and in drill-down detail
- Blame blocks remain the provenance and detail unit even though the UI is file-row-based
- The first overview should degrade gracefully to plain blame behavior when optional Entire enrichment data is unavailable

## Detail Views

### Checkpoint Detail

When a blamed commit links to an Entire checkpoint, the detail screen should show checkpoint-first information:

- Checkpoint ID
- Commit linkage
- Agent
- Summary if generated
- Fallback summary when no generated summary exists
- Files touched
- Session count
- Token usage when available
- File-scoped diff for the selected file

The checkpoint detail screen should have clear visual separation between:

- checkpoint metadata
- the interactive session list
- the file diff

It should then provide a path into session-level detail.

For multi-session checkpoints, the UI must not pretend there is always one obvious originating session. The checkpoint screen is the correct place to expose that ambiguity honestly.

The session list should be interactive, not a static blob of text. The user should be able to move between sessions and drill into one explicitly.

### Session Detail

Session detail is a drill-down from checkpoint detail.

For the prototype, this view should reuse or closely mirror current `entire explain --checkpoint` rendering rather than inventing a completely new transcript presentation layer.

Concretely:

- Transcript content should be rendered in the same condensed, human-readable style as `entire explain --checkpoint`, not as raw transcript JSON
- Tool-call-heavy transcript stretches should be collapsed by default in the interactive session view
- The user should be able to expand or collapse those tool-call groups on demand
- Tool-call groups should be rendered as separate bordered sections, not only as inline text
- `tab` should move forward between tool-call sections
- `shift+tab` should move backward between tool-call sections
- `e` should expand or collapse only the currently selected tool-call section
- When a tool-call section gains focus through tabbing, the viewport should scroll to keep that section visible

This keeps the session view legible enough for demos while still preserving access to the underlying transcript flow.

### Git Commit Fallback Detail

When a blamed commit has no Entire linkage, the detail screen should show:

- Commit hash
- Author
- Date
- Commit subject
- File-scoped diff for the selected file in that commit

This keeps the command valuable across mixed histories where some commits came from Entire sessions and others did not.

For the diff presentation, simple whole-diff syntax highlighting is not sufficient. The more useful rendering direction is:

- preserve diff structure and hunk headers
- show explicit green/red change indicators for added and removed lines
- syntax-highlight the code portion of changed lines where practical

## Reuse Opportunities

The prototype should reuse existing code where possible:

- Commit-to-checkpoint resolution and trailer parsing from `entire explain`
- Checkpoint summary and session readers from the `checkpoint` package
- Pager behavior from `entire explain`
- Bubble Tea browse/detail patterns from `search_tui.go`

The new command should avoid introducing a parallel metadata resolution stack when the `explain` path already has the local building blocks needed for prototype scope.

## Risks

### Provenance Join Ambiguity

The hardest part is not rendering but joining:

`blame commit -> Entire-Checkpoint trailer -> checkpoint -> session detail`

This join is straightforward when one blamed commit has one checkpoint and one relevant session. It becomes ambiguous when a checkpoint contains multiple sessions.

The design handles this by making checkpoint detail the first drill-down level instead of jumping directly to a session.

### Overreaching On Highlighting

Syntax highlighting adds complexity in wrapping, width calculation, viewport scrolling, and theme selection. The prototype still accepts that cost because highlighted code materially improves the demo and better matches the reference experience.

To keep the scope controlled:

- Use an existing pure-Go highlighting library rather than building a custom lexer path
- Restrict built-in highlighting to the TUI code pane
- Continue relying on pager-based highlighting for non-interactive output
- Fall back gracefully to unhighlighted text if no lexer can be identified

There are now two distinct highlighting problems:

- source-file highlighting in the main interactive file view
- diff-aware highlighting in detail views

The second is more complex because useful diff presentation requires preserving add/remove semantics in addition to code coloring.

### Performance On Large Files

Blame parsing on very large files may be slow. The prototype accepts raw local blame latency rather than adding indexing or progressive loading upfront.

If performance is poor in practice, that should be addressed in a later iteration based on observed bottlenecks.

## Deferred Questions

The following questions are intentionally deferred rather than solved in the prototype:

- Whether the static first view should more closely mimic exact `git blame` formatting or keep a slightly more explicit Entire-oriented gutter
- Whether Git fallback detail should show the full commit patch or only the selected file diff
- Whether future `--json` output should model lines, blocks, or commit-grouped blocks
- Whether later versions should support revision arguments, rename/copy tracking, or remote metadata fetching
- Whether the no-arg file browser should later hide dotfiles by default or support filtering/toggling
- Whether interactive file opening should support searching/filtering within the file browser
- Whether a future `--browse` flag should exist separately from `--interactive`, or whether the current no-arg browser entry is sufficient

## Recommended Implementation Phasing

Phase 1:

- Add `entire why <path>` in non-interactive mode
- Parse local blame output into contiguous blocks
- Enrich blocks with local Entire metadata when available
- Add checkpoint detail and Git fallback detail
- Reuse pager behavior

Phase 2:

- Add interactive TUI on top of the same display model
- Rework the first screen so the file itself is the primary browsing surface
- Add syntax-highlighted code rendering in the TUI code pane, preferably using Chroma-backed ANSI output
- Add checkpoint detail, session list drill-down, and session transcript rendering modeled after `entire explain --checkpoint`
- Add general pager navigation shortcuts and default tool-call collapsing in session detail

Phase 3:

- Add no-arg interactive entry through a file browser rooted at `pwd`
- Preserve browser state when returning from a file
- Polish visual layout, colors, and diff presentation based on demo feedback

Across those phases, `entire why` should preserve its richer multi-pane interaction model while converging toward the same documented control vocabulary and general TUI conventions used by other interactive Entire commands.

This sequencing reflects what the prototype exploration actually taught: the file-primary interactive view and the checkpoint/session drill-down are the core of the feature, and the browser entrypoint is a useful but secondary layer on top.

When Entire metadata is available for the blamed commit, that Entire context should be visible in the main screen by default so users can immediately understand not just who last touched the code, but also whether the change came through an Entire checkpoint and which agent or session context was involved.

The intended layout is:

- Left side or metadata gutter: blame-oriented identity fields such as short commit hash, author, checkpoint ID, agent, and line number
- Right side or code pane: the source line itself

In other words, the Entire-specific fields belong in the default scanning surface of the first screen, not only in an expanded detail view.

Each visible file row should expose:

- File line number
- Short commit hash
- Author
- Checkpoint ID, when present
- Agent name, when present
- The source line itself

For Entire-linked lines, the main screen should aim to surface these fields directly in the primary browsing experience:

- Entire checkpoint ID
- AI agent used
- Short AI-generated summary, when already available
- Fallback summary text when no generated summary exists

The screen should therefore feel like "blame plus Entire provenance" rather than "blame with a separate details screen."

For non-Entire commits, those same metadata slots may be blank, replaced with placeholders, or omitted in a visually consistent way, but the layout should still preserve the same overall scanning model.

Because summary text is often too wide to show next to every line without destroying file readability, the interactive view may surface summary in selected-line metadata rather than in every row of the gutter.

### Non-Interactive Mode

Non-interactive mode should be the baseline behavior.

It should:

- Produce a readable text rendering of the file line-by-line
- Work when stdout is piped
- Work in accessibility mode
- Preserve compatibility with pager-based presentation such as `less` or `delta`
- Support line-restricted views via `--lines` / `-L`

If output is long, the command should use the same pager strategy already used by `entire explain`.

For non-interactive output, pager-based syntax highlighting remains acceptable and desirable. Users who already route CLI output through tools such as `delta` should be able to benefit from that setup.

The current command contract is intentionally split:

- interactive terminal without overrides: default to the TUI
- non-interactive, piped, or accessibility mode: default to static output
- `--interactive`: force the TUI and fail clearly if a real interactive terminal is unavailable
- `--no-pager`: keep static output but bypass pager integration

In implementation terms, the TUI path should require all of the following:

- accessibility mode is not enabled
- output is attached to a terminal-capable writer
- interactive prompting is possible under the CLI's normal `CanPromptInteractively()` rules

### Interactive Mode

When a real interactive shell is available, the command should offer a TUI.

The TUI should reuse established Bubble Tea interaction patterns already used elsewhere in the CLI:

- Optional file-browser mode when `entire why` is invoked without a path
- Browse mode for the full file
- Detail mode for checkpoint or commit detail
- Session detail mode
- Viewport scrolling for long content
- `j` and `k`, plus arrow keys, for movement
- `enter` or space to open detail
- `esc` or `q` to go back

The visible help text should prioritize accessible/default controls:

- arrow keys
- `enter`
- `esc`

Vim-style aliases should still exist, but they do not need to be shown in help text. The intended hidden alias policy is:

- `h` = back
- `j` = down
- `k` = up
- `l` = open / drill down / confirm

This means the documented controls remain accessibility-first while users familiar with vim-like navigation can still rely on the same directional vocabulary across views.

The TUI should include syntax highlighting in the code pane for the prototype.

The recommended approach is to use a pure-Go highlighter that emits ANSI-colored terminal text for direct rendering inside Bubble Tea viewports. The leading candidate is Chroma because it is pure Go, supports many languages, and can format to terminal color output. Markdown-focused renderers such as Glamour are less suitable as the primary engine because this screen is fundamentally a source-code browser, not a markdown document renderer.

Syntax highlighting should be applied only to the code pane, not to the metadata gutter. The metadata side should remain styled via Lip Gloss so the two layers remain visually distinct.

In the interactive view, the selected line may also drive a compact metadata header showing richer fields such as date and summary, while the scrollable body stays focused on the file itself.

The interactive view should favor code readability over stuffing every Entire field into the per-line gutter. The settled layout direction is:

- A compact left gutter for the file view with commit hash, author, checkpoint ID, and line number
- A richer top metadata bar for the currently selected line, using labeled fields such as commit, author, date, checkpoint, agent, and summary
- Detail screens that use clearly separated sections instead of one continuous text wall

General pager-style shortcuts should be supported in all TUI views:

- `g` jumps to the top
- `G` jumps to the bottom

Checkpoint detail should use explicit focusable panes rather than treating the entire screen as one undifferentiated scroll surface. The current pane model is:

- `Sessions`
- `Generated Checkpoint Summary`
- `File Diff`

`tab` cycles forward through those panes when more than one is present. The focused pane should:

- receive the active bordered-panel treatment
- own `j` / `k` or arrow-key scrolling when it is a scrollable pane
- expand to show materially more content than the unfocused panes

Unfocused panes may render as previews rather than full sections. In particular:

- the session list may show only the first few rows plus a “more sessions” hint
- the generated summary may show only an initial preview when unfocused
- the diff may show only an initial preview when unfocused

### Interactive Entry Without a Path

If `entire why` is invoked with no path in an interactive shell, it should start in a lightweight file browser rooted at the current working directory.

This browser should:

- Show all files and directories, including dotfiles
- Sort directories before files
- Allow directory traversal with `j`/`k`, arrows, `enter`, and `h` or `backspace`
- Preserve browser directory and cursor position when the user opens a file and later returns from the why view

If `entire why` is invoked with no path in a non-interactive environment, it should return an error rather than attempting to print a directory listing.

If `--interactive` is supplied explicitly, the same rule should apply: failure is preferable to silently falling back to static output.

## Data Flow

The command should follow this pipeline:

1. Validate that the target path exists at `HEAD`
2. If `--lines` / `-L` is present, parse numeric-only input:
   - `N`
   - `start-end`
   Both `-L` and `--lines` should accept either form.
3. Run `git blame --line-porcelain -- <path>` against `HEAD`
   - when a line range is present, pass it through as `git blame -L <git-range>`
3. Parse blame output into line records
4. Collapse adjacent lines with the same blamed commit into contiguous blame blocks
5. For each unique blamed commit:
   - Resolve the local commit object
   - Parse `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer if present
   - If linked, read checkpoint summary and latest relevant session metadata from local checkpoint storage
   - If the blamed commit object is missing locally, or checkpoint/session metadata is partially unavailable, degrade to plain blame metadata for the affected lines instead of aborting the whole overview
6. Flatten blame blocks into a full-file row model that preserves the owning block for each source line
7. Detect or derive the file language for syntax highlighting, preferably from the target filename and falling back safely when unknown
8. Render syntax-highlighted code lines for the code pane in interactive mode
9. Render either:
   - a static text blame-like file view, or
   - an interactive Bubble Tea model backed by the same row data
10. In the no-arg interactive case, resolve the target path through a TUI file browser before loading blame data

The key invariants are:

- Git determines which commit last touched the current line
- Entire determines what extra context should be surfaced alongside that commit in the first view and in drill-down detail
- Blame blocks remain the provenance and detail unit even though the UI is file-row-based
- The first overview should degrade gracefully to plain blame behavior when optional Entire enrichment data is unavailable

## Detail Views

### Checkpoint Detail

When a blamed commit links to an Entire checkpoint, the detail screen should show checkpoint-first information:

- Checkpoint ID
- Commit linkage
- Agent
- Summary if generated
- Fallback summary when no generated summary exists
- Files touched
- Session count
- Token usage when available
- File-scoped diff for the selected file

The checkpoint detail screen should have clear visual separation between:

- checkpoint metadata
- the interactive session list
- the file diff

It should then provide a path into session-level detail.

For multi-session checkpoints, the UI must not pretend there is always one obvious originating session. The checkpoint screen is the correct place to expose that ambiguity honestly.

The session list should be interactive, not a static blob of text. The user should be able to move between sessions and drill into one explicitly.

### Session Detail

Session detail is a drill-down from checkpoint detail.

For the prototype, this view should reuse or closely mirror current `entire explain --checkpoint` rendering rather than inventing a completely new transcript presentation layer.

Concretely:

- Transcript content should be rendered in the same condensed, human-readable style as `entire explain --checkpoint`, not as raw transcript JSON
- Tool-call-heavy transcript stretches should be collapsed by default in the interactive session view
- The user should be able to expand or collapse those tool-call groups on demand
- Tool-call groups should be rendered as separate bordered sections, not only as inline text
- `tab` should move forward between tool-call sections
- `shift+tab` should move backward between tool-call sections
- `e` should expand or collapse only the currently selected tool-call section
- When a tool-call section gains focus through tabbing, the viewport should scroll to keep that section visible

This keeps the session view legible enough for demos while still preserving access to the underlying transcript flow.

### Git Commit Fallback Detail

When a blamed commit has no Entire linkage, the detail screen should show:

- Commit hash
- Author
- Date
- Commit subject
- File-scoped diff for the selected file in that commit

This keeps the command valuable across mixed histories where some commits came from Entire sessions and others did not.

For the diff presentation, simple whole-diff syntax highlighting is not sufficient. The more useful rendering direction is:

- preserve diff structure and hunk headers
- show explicit green/red change indicators for added and removed lines
- syntax-highlight the code portion of changed lines where practical

## Reuse Opportunities

The prototype should reuse existing code where possible:

- Commit-to-checkpoint resolution and trailer parsing from `entire explain`
- Checkpoint summary and session readers from the `checkpoint` package
- Pager behavior from `entire explain`
- Bubble Tea browse/detail patterns from `search_tui.go`

The new command should avoid introducing a parallel metadata resolution stack when the `explain` path already has the local building blocks needed for prototype scope.

## Risks

### Provenance Join Ambiguity

The hardest part is not rendering but joining:

`blame commit -> Entire-Checkpoint trailer -> checkpoint -> session detail`

This join is straightforward when one blamed commit has one checkpoint and one relevant session. It becomes ambiguous when a checkpoint contains multiple sessions.

The design handles this by making checkpoint detail the first drill-down level instead of jumping directly to a session.

### Overreaching On Highlighting

Syntax highlighting adds complexity in wrapping, width calculation, viewport scrolling, and theme selection. The prototype still accepts that cost because highlighted code materially improves the demo and better matches the reference experience.

To keep the scope controlled:

- Use an existing pure-Go highlighting library rather than building a custom lexer path
- Restrict built-in highlighting to the TUI code pane
- Continue relying on pager-based highlighting for non-interactive output
- Fall back gracefully to unhighlighted text if no lexer can be identified

There are now two distinct highlighting problems:

- source-file highlighting in the main interactive file view
- diff-aware highlighting in detail views

The second is more complex because useful diff presentation requires preserving add/remove semantics in addition to code coloring.

### Performance On Large Files

Blame parsing on very large files may be slow. The prototype accepts raw local blame latency rather than adding indexing or progressive loading upfront.

If performance is poor in practice, that should be addressed in a later iteration based on observed bottlenecks.

## Deferred Questions

The following questions are intentionally deferred rather than solved in the prototype:

- Whether the static first view should more closely mimic exact `git blame` formatting or keep a slightly more explicit Entire-oriented gutter
- Whether Git fallback detail should show the full commit patch or only the selected file diff
- Whether future `--json` output should model lines, blocks, or commit-grouped blocks
- Whether later versions should support revision arguments, rename/copy tracking, or remote metadata fetching
- Whether the no-arg file browser should later hide dotfiles by default or support filtering/toggling
- Whether interactive file opening should support searching/filtering within the file browser
- Whether a future `--browse` flag should exist separately from `--interactive`, or whether the current no-arg browser entry is sufficient

## Recommended Implementation Phasing

Phase 1:

- Add `entire why <path>` in non-interactive mode
- Parse local blame output into contiguous blocks
- Enrich blocks with local Entire metadata when available
- Add checkpoint detail and Git fallback detail
- Reuse pager behavior

Phase 2:

- Add interactive TUI on top of the same display model
- Rework the first screen so the file itself is the primary browsing surface
- Add syntax-highlighted code rendering in the TUI code pane, preferably using Chroma-backed ANSI output
- Add checkpoint detail, session list drill-down, and session transcript rendering modeled after `entire explain --checkpoint`
- Add general pager navigation shortcuts and default tool-call collapsing in session detail

Phase 3:

- Add no-arg interactive entry through a file browser rooted at `pwd`
- Preserve browser state when returning from a file
- Polish visual layout, colors, and diff presentation based on demo feedback

Across those phases, `entire why` should preserve its richer multi-pane interaction model while converging toward the same documented control vocabulary and general TUI conventions used by other interactive Entire commands.

This sequencing reflects what the prototype exploration actually taught: the file-primary interactive view and the checkpoint/session drill-down are the core of the feature, and the browser entrypoint is a useful but secondary layer on top.

// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit using native git CLI.
// This is much faster than go-git's worktree.Status() which scans the entire
// working tree. `git diff --cached --name-only` uses native git's optimized index
// and filesystem monitors.
//
// Returns (non-nil empty slice, nil) when no files are staged — callers can
// distinguish "no staged files" from "error resolving staged files" (nil, err).
func getStagedFiles(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root: %w", err)
	}

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only")
	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
	output, err := cmd.Output()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("git diff --cached: %w", err)
	}

	staged := []string{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), "\n") {
		if line != "" {
			staged = append(staged, line)
		}
	}
	return staged, nil
}

// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
// Reads prompt.txt directly from the shadow branch tree instead of parsing the full
// transcript (which involves token counting, context generation, etc.).
// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(_ context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	// Read prompt.txt directly from the shadow branch tree.
	// Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n" — extract the last one.
	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
	promptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.PromptFileName
	file, err := tree.File(promptPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	content, err := file.Contents()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	return extractLastPrompt(content)
}

// extractLastPrompt returns the last non-empty prompt from prompt.txt content.
// Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n".
func extractLastPrompt(content string) string {
	if content == "" {
		return ""
	}

	prompts := strings.Split(content, "\n\n---\n\n")
	// Iterate backwards to find the last non-empty prompt
	for i := len(prompts) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(prompts[i])
		if cleaned != "" && !isOnlySeparators(cleaned) {
			return cleaned
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// HandleTurnEnd dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted when an agent turn ends.
// The primary job is to finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
//
// During a turn, PostCommit writes provisional transcript data (whatever was available
// at commit time). HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript
// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.
//

func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(ctx context.Context, state *SessionState) error { //nolint:unparam // error return is part of the hook contract; callers check it
	// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
	//
	// IMPORTANT: This is best-effort - errors are logged but don't fail the hook.
	// Failing here would prevent session cleanup and could leave state inconsistent.
	// The provisional transcript from PostCommit is already persisted, so the
	// checkpoint isn't lost - it just won't have the complete transcript.
	errCount := s.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(ctx, state)
	if errCount > 0 {
		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "HandleTurnEnd completed with errors (best-effort)",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.Int("error_count", errCount),
		)
	}
	return nil
}

func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(ctx context.Context, state *SessionState) int {

		return 0 // No mid-turn commits to finalize

	// agent relocated it mid-session (e.g., Cursor CLI flat → nested layout change).

			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),

		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped

			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),

		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped

		msg := "finalize: empty transcript, skipping"
		if err != nil {

		}

			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
			slog.Any("error", err),

	}

	if err != nil {

			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}

	prompts := readPromptsFromShadowBranch(ctx, repo, state)
	if len(prompts) == 0 {
		prompts = readPromptsFromFilesystem(ctx, state.SessionID)
	}

	// Redact secrets before writing — matches WriteCommitted behavior.
	// The live transcript on disk contains raw content; redaction must happen
	// before anything is persisted to the metadata branch.
	fullTranscript, err = redact.JSONLBytes(fullTranscript)
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript redaction failed, skipping",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}
	for i, p := range prompts {
		prompts[i] = redact.String(p)
	}

	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

	// Evaluate v2 flag once before the loop to avoid re-reading settings per checkpoint
	var v2Store *checkpoint.V2GitStore
	if settings.IsCheckpointsV2Enabled(logCtx) {
		v2Store = checkpoint.NewV2GitStore(repo)
	}

	// Update each checkpoint with the full transcript
	for _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {
		cpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)
		if parseErr != nil {
			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping",
				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
				slog.String("error", parseErr.Error()),
			)
			errCount++
			continue
		}

		updateOpts := checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{
			CheckpointID: cpID,
			SessionID:    state.SessionID,
			Transcript:   fullTranscript,
			Prompts:      prompts,
			Agent:        state.AgentType,
		}

		updateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(ctx, updateOpts)
		if updateErr != nil {
			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to update checkpoint",
				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
				slog.String("error", updateErr.Error()),
			)
			errCount++
			continue
		}

		// Dual-write: update v2 refs when enabled
		if v2Store != nil {
			if v2Err := v2Store.UpdateCommitted(logCtx, updateOpts); v2Err != nil {
				logging.Warn(logCtx, "v2 dual-write update failed",
					slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
					slog.String("error", v2Err.Error()),
				)
			}
		}

		logging.Info(logCtx, "finalize: checkpoint updated with full transcript",
			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		)
	}

	// Clear turn checkpoint IDs. Do NOT update CheckpointTranscriptStart here — it was
	// already set correctly by PostCommit: condenseAndUpdateState sets it to the total
	// transcript lines when condensing, and carryForwardToNewShadowBranch resets it to 0
	// when carry-forward is active. Overwriting here would break carry-forward by making
	// sessionHasNewContent think the transcript is fully consumed (no growth).
	state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil

	return errCount
}

// filesChangedInCommit returns the set of files changed in a commit using git diff-tree.
// Uses the git CLI for faster performance vs go-git tree walks (lower constant factors).
// Falls back to go-git tree walk if git diff-tree fails, since an empty result would
// break downstream condensation and carry-forward logic.
func filesChangedInCommit(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, commit *object.Commit, headTree, parentTree *object.Tree) map[string]struct{} {
	var parentHash string
	if commit.NumParents() > 0 {
		parentHash = commit.ParentHashes[0].String()
	}
	result, err := gitops.DiffTreeFiles(ctx, repoDir, parentHash, commit.Hash.String())
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(ctx, "post-commit: git diff-tree failed, falling back to tree walk",
			slog.String("commit", commit.Hash.String()),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return filesChangedInCommitFallback(ctx, headTree, parentTree)
	}
	return result
}

// filesChangedInCommitFallback uses go-git tree walks to compute changed files.
// Slower than git diff-tree but doesn't depend on an external process.
func filesChangedInCommitFallback(ctx context.Context, headTree, parentTree *object.Tree) map[string]struct{} {
	files, err := getAllChangedFilesBetweenTreesSlow(ctx, parentTree, headTree)
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(ctx, "post-commit: tree walk fallback also failed; condensation and carry-forward may be affected",
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return make(map[string]struct{})
	}
	result := make(map[string]struct{}, len(files))
	for _, f := range files {
		result[f] = struct{}{}
	}
	return result
}

// subtractFiles returns files that are NOT in the exclude set.
func subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string {
	var remaining []string
	for _, f := range files {
		if _, excluded := exclude[f]; !excluded {
			remaining = append(remaining, f)
		}
	}
	return remaining
}

// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
	ctx context.Context,
	repo *git.Repository,
	state *SessionState,
	remainingFiles []string,
) {
	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(ctx, checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
		MetadataDir:       "",
		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
	})
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return
	}
	if result.Skipped {
		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		)
		return
	}

	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
	//   the full transcript, which could be large
	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.
	state.StepCount = 1
	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
	state.CheckpointTranscriptSize = 0
	state.LastCheckpointID = ""
	// NOTE: TurnCheckpointIDs is intentionally NOT cleared here. Those checkpoint
	// IDs from earlier in the turn still need finalization with the full transcript
	// when HandleTurnEnd runs at stop time.

	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: carried forward remaining files",
		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remainingFiles)),
	)
}

cmd/entire/cli/agent/cursor/AGENT.md:5:The `agent` binary supports hooks via `.cursor/hooks.json` and stores JSONL transcripts in a predictable location. The existing Cursor agent implementation in this package already handles both IDE and CLI modes. The CLI fires `sessionStart`, `sessionEnd`, `preToolUse`, and `postToolUse` hooks in headless (`-p`) mode. In interactive mode, `beforeSubmitPrompt` and `stop` also fire.

Only `sessionStart`, `sessionEnd`, and tool-use hooks fire. This means E2E tests using `RunPrompt` (headless) will not get `TurnStart`/`TurnEnd` events — only `SessionStart`/`SessionEnd`. Interactive tmux-based tests get the full lifecycle.

// getStagedFiles returns a list of files staged for commit using native git CLI.
// This is much faster than go-git's worktree.Status() which scans the entire
// working tree. `git diff --cached --name-only` uses native git's optimized index
// and filesystem monitors.
//
// Returns (non-nil empty slice, nil) when no files are staged — callers can
// distinguish "no staged files" from "error resolving staged files" (nil, err).
func getStagedFiles(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
	repoRoot, err := paths.WorktreeRoot(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("resolve worktree root: %w", err)
	}

	cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", "diff", "--cached", "--name-only")
	cmd.Dir = repoRoot
	output, err := cmd.Output()
	if err != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("git diff --cached: %w", err)
	}

	staged := []string{}
	for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(output)), "\n") {
		if line != "" {
			staged = append(staged, line)
		}
	}
	return staged, nil
}

// getLastPrompt retrieves the most recent user prompt from a session's shadow branch.
// Reads prompt.txt directly from the shadow branch tree instead of parsing the full
// transcript (which involves token counting, context generation, etc.).
// Returns empty string if no prompt can be retrieved.
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) getLastPrompt(_ context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) string {
	shadowBranchName := getShadowBranchNameForCommit(state.BaseCommit, state.WorktreeID)
	refName := plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(shadowBranchName)
	ref, err := repo.Reference(refName, true)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	// Read prompt.txt directly from the shadow branch tree.
	// Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n" — extract the last one.
	metadataDir := paths.EntireMetadataDir + "/" + state.SessionID
	promptPath := metadataDir + "/" + paths.PromptFileName
	file, err := tree.File(promptPath)
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	content, err := file.Contents()
	if err != nil {
		return ""
	}

	return extractLastPrompt(content)
}

// extractLastPrompt returns the last non-empty prompt from prompt.txt content.
// Prompts are separated by "\n\n---\n\n".
func extractLastPrompt(content string) string {
	if content == "" {
		return ""
	}

	prompts := strings.Split(content, "\n\n---\n\n")
	// Iterate backwards to find the last non-empty prompt
	for i := len(prompts) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		cleaned := strings.TrimSpace(prompts[i])
		if cleaned != "" && !isOnlySeparators(cleaned) {
			return cleaned
		}
	}
	return ""
}

func readPromptsFromShadowBranch(_ context.Context, repo *git.Repository, state *SessionState) []string {

// HandleTurnEnd dispatches strategy-specific actions emitted when an agent turn ends.
// The primary job is to finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
//
// During a turn, PostCommit writes provisional transcript data (whatever was available
// at commit time). HandleTurnEnd replaces that with the complete session transcript
// (from prompt to stop event), ensuring every checkpoint has the full context.
//

func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) HandleTurnEnd(ctx context.Context, state *SessionState) error { //nolint:unparam // error return is part of the hook contract; callers check it
	// Finalize all checkpoints from this turn with the full transcript.
	//
	// IMPORTANT: This is best-effort - errors are logged but don't fail the hook.
	// Failing here would prevent session cleanup and could leave state inconsistent.
	// The provisional transcript from PostCommit is already persisted, so the
	// checkpoint isn't lost - it just won't have the complete transcript.
	errCount := s.finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(ctx, state)
	if errCount > 0 {
		logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "HandleTurnEnd completed with errors (best-effort)",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.Int("error_count", errCount),
		)
	}
	return nil
}

// finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints replaces the provisional transcript in each checkpoint
// created during this turn with the full session transcript.
//
// This is called at turn end (stop hook). During the turn, PostCommit wrote whatever
// transcript was available at commit time. Now we have the complete transcript and
// replace it so every checkpoint has the full prompt-to-stop context.
//
// Returns the number of errors encountered (best-effort: continues processing on error).
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) finalizeAllTurnCheckpoints(ctx context.Context, state *SessionState) int {
	if len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs) == 0 {
		return 0 // No mid-turn commits to finalize
	}

	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")

	logging.Info(logCtx, "finalizing turn checkpoints with full transcript",
		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		slog.Int("checkpoint_count", len(state.TurnCheckpointIDs)),
	)

	errCount := 0

	// Read full transcript from live transcript file, re-resolving the path if the
	// agent relocated it mid-session (e.g., Cursor CLI flat → nested layout change).
	if state.TranscriptPath == "" {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: no transcript path, skipping",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}

	transcriptPath, resolveErr := resolveTranscriptPath(state)
	if resolveErr != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript path resolution failed, skipping",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.Any("error", resolveErr),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}

	fullTranscript, err := os.ReadFile(transcriptPath) //nolint:gosec // path validated by resolveTranscriptPath
	if err != nil || len(fullTranscript) == 0 {
		msg := "finalize: empty transcript, skipping"
		if err != nil {
			msg = "finalize: failed to read transcript, skipping"
		}
		logging.Warn(logCtx, msg,
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("transcript_path", state.TranscriptPath),
			slog.Any("error", err),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}

	// Open repository (needed for shadow branch prompt reading and checkpoint store)
	repo, err := OpenRepository(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to open repository",
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}

	prompts := readPromptsFromShadowBranch(ctx, repo, state)
	if len(prompts) == 0 {
		prompts = readPromptsFromFilesystem(ctx, state.SessionID)
	}

	// Redact secrets before writing — matches WriteCommitted behavior.
	// The live transcript on disk contains raw content; redaction must happen
	// before anything is persisted to the metadata branch.
	fullTranscript, err = redact.JSONLBytes(fullTranscript)
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: transcript redaction failed, skipping",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil
		return 1 // Count as error - all checkpoints will be skipped
	}
	for i, p := range prompts {
		prompts[i] = redact.String(p)
	}

	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

	// Evaluate v2 flag once before the loop to avoid re-reading settings per checkpoint
	var v2Store *checkpoint.V2GitStore
	if settings.IsCheckpointsV2Enabled(logCtx) {
		v2Store = checkpoint.NewV2GitStore(repo)
	}

	// Update each checkpoint with the full transcript
	for _, cpIDStr := range state.TurnCheckpointIDs {
		cpID, parseErr := id.NewCheckpointID(cpIDStr)
		if parseErr != nil {
			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: invalid checkpoint ID, skipping",
				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
				slog.String("error", parseErr.Error()),
			)
			errCount++
			continue
		}

		updateOpts := checkpoint.UpdateCommittedOptions{
			CheckpointID: cpID,
			SessionID:    state.SessionID,
			Transcript:   fullTranscript,
			Prompts:      prompts,
			Agent:        state.AgentType,
		}

		updateErr := store.UpdateCommitted(ctx, updateOpts)
		if updateErr != nil {
			logging.Warn(logCtx, "finalize: failed to update checkpoint",
				slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
				slog.String("error", updateErr.Error()),
			)
			errCount++
			continue
		}

		// Dual-write: update v2 refs when enabled
		if v2Store != nil {
			if v2Err := v2Store.UpdateCommitted(logCtx, updateOpts); v2Err != nil {
				logging.Warn(logCtx, "v2 dual-write update failed",
					slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
					slog.String("error", v2Err.Error()),
				)
			}
		}

		logging.Info(logCtx, "finalize: checkpoint updated with full transcript",
			slog.String("checkpoint_id", cpIDStr),
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		)
	}

	// Clear turn checkpoint IDs. Do NOT update CheckpointTranscriptStart here — it was
	// already set correctly by PostCommit: condenseAndUpdateState sets it to the total
	// transcript lines when condensing, and carryForwardToNewShadowBranch resets it to 0
	// when carry-forward is active. Overwriting here would break carry-forward by making
	// sessionHasNewContent think the transcript is fully consumed (no growth).
	state.TurnCheckpointIDs = nil

	return errCount
}

// filesChangedInCommit returns the set of files changed in a commit using git diff-tree.
// Uses the git CLI for faster performance vs go-git tree walks (lower constant factors).
// Falls back to go-git tree walk if git diff-tree fails, since an empty result would
// break downstream condensation and carry-forward logic.
func filesChangedInCommit(ctx context.Context, repoDir string, commit *object.Commit, headTree, parentTree *object.Tree) map[string]struct{} {
	var parentHash string
	if commit.NumParents() > 0 {
		parentHash = commit.ParentHashes[0].String()
	}
	result, err := gitops.DiffTreeFiles(ctx, repoDir, parentHash, commit.Hash.String())
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(ctx, "post-commit: git diff-tree failed, falling back to tree walk",
			slog.String("commit", commit.Hash.String()),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return filesChangedInCommitFallback(ctx, headTree, parentTree)
	}
	return result
}

// filesChangedInCommitFallback uses go-git tree walks to compute changed files.
// Slower than git diff-tree but doesn't depend on an external process.
func filesChangedInCommitFallback(ctx context.Context, headTree, parentTree *object.Tree) map[string]struct{} {
	files, err := getAllChangedFilesBetweenTreesSlow(ctx, parentTree, headTree)
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(ctx, "post-commit: tree walk fallback also failed; condensation and carry-forward may be affected",
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return make(map[string]struct{})
	}
	result := make(map[string]struct{}, len(files))
	for _, f := range files {
		result[f] = struct{}{}
	}
	return result
}

// subtractFiles returns files that are NOT in the exclude set.
func subtractFiles(files []string, exclude map[string]struct{}) []string {
	var remaining []string
	for _, f := range files {
		if _, excluded := exclude[f]; !excluded {
			remaining = append(remaining, f)
		}
	}
	return remaining
}

// carryForwardToNewShadowBranch creates a new shadow branch at the current HEAD
// containing the remaining uncommitted files and all session metadata.
// This enables the next commit to get its own unique checkpoint.
func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) carryForwardToNewShadowBranch(
	ctx context.Context,
	repo *git.Repository,
	state *SessionState,
	remainingFiles []string,
) {
	logCtx := logging.WithComponent(ctx, "checkpoint")
	store := checkpoint.NewGitStore(repo)

	// Don't include metadata directory in carry-forward. The carry-forward branch
	// only needs to preserve file content for comparison - not the transcript.
	// Including the transcript would cause sessionHasNewContent to always return true
	// because CheckpointTranscriptStart is reset to 0 for carry-forward.
	result, err := store.WriteTemporary(ctx, checkpoint.WriteTemporaryOptions{
		SessionID:         state.SessionID,
		BaseCommit:        state.BaseCommit,
		WorktreeID:        state.WorktreeID,
		ModifiedFiles:     remainingFiles,
		MetadataDir:       "",
		MetadataDirAbs:    "",
		CommitMessage:     "carry forward: uncommitted session files",
		IsFirstCheckpoint: false,
	})
	if err != nil {
		logging.Warn(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward failed",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
			slog.String("error", err.Error()),
		)
		return
	}
	if result.Skipped {
		logging.Debug(logCtx, "post-commit: carry-forward skipped (no changes)",
			slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		)
		return
	}

	// Update state for the carry-forward checkpoint.
	// CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0 is intentional: each checkpoint is self-contained with
	// the full transcript. This trades storage efficiency for simplicity:
	// - Pro: Each checkpoint is independently readable without needing to stitch together
	//   multiple checkpoints to understand the session history
	// - Con: For long sessions with multiple partial commits, each checkpoint includes
	//   the full transcript, which could be large
	// An alternative would be incremental checkpoints (only new content since last condensation),
	// but this would complicate checkpoint retrieval and require careful tracking of dependencies.
	state.StepCount = 1
	state.CheckpointTranscriptStart = 0
	state.CheckpointTranscriptSize = 0
	state.LastCheckpointID = ""
	// NOTE: TurnCheckpointIDs is intentionally NOT cleared here. Those checkpoint
	// IDs from earlier in the turn still need finalization with the full transcript
	// when HandleTurnEnd runs at stop time.

	logging.Info(logCtx, "post-commit: carried forward remaining files",
		slog.String("session_id", state.SessionID),
		slog.Int("remaining_files", len(remainingFiles)),
	)
}

I read the spec and the relevant implementation paths: [spec](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-21-entire-why-design.md:1), [root command registration](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/cmd/entire/cli/root.go:31), [explain checkpoint/pager logic](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:215), [search TUI patterns](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/cmd/entire/cli/search_tui.go:1), [terminal gating](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/interactive.go:27), and [checkpoint data types](/Users/pfleidi/entire/cli/.worktrees/feat/entire-why/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/checkpoint.go:419). `git status --short` is clean.

**Recommended Approach**

Use a core `why` data model first, then layer UI/detail features on top. I would not route through `runExplainCheckpointWithLookup` because it fetches remote metadata on miss, while the spec requires local-only resolution. Reuse lower-level explain/checkpoint helpers instead.

**PR 1: Hidden Baseline Command**

Add hidden `entire why` with:

- `entire why <path>`
- `-L` / `--lines`
- `--interactive`
- `--no-pager`
- `Hidden: true` in Cobra registration
- `git blame --line-porcelain -- <path>` parsing
- contiguous blame block collapse
- static blame-like output with pager reuse
- simple scrollable TUI over the full file, with line selection and `j/k`/arrows
- no checkpoint/session details yet
- no no-arg file browser yet; no path returns a clear temporary error

Tests: line range parser, blame parser fixtures, block collapse, hidden command registration, static rendering, TUI movement model.

**PR 2: Entire Enrichment In Overview**

Add local commit enrichment:

- parse `Entire-Checkpoint` trailers from blamed commits
- resolve local checkpoint summary/session metadata through checkpoint stores
- show checkpoint ID, agent, and summary/fallback text
- enrich static output and selected-line TUI header
- degrade per-commit when metadata is missing or malformed

Tests: plain commit, commit with trailer and metadata, trailer with missing checkpoint, multi-session checkpoint overview fields.

**PR 3: Detail Navigation Without Session Drilldown**

Add `enter`/space drilldown from a selected blame block:

- checkpoint detail when `Entire-Checkpoint` exists
- generic Git commit fallback otherwise
- file-scoped diff for the selected path
- `esc`/`q` back behavior
- checkpoint detail shows ID, commit, agent, summary/fallback, files, session count, tokens when present

Tests: key transitions, checkpoint detail rendering, Git fallback rendering, file-scoped diff command behavior.

**PR 4: Checkpoint Detail Pane Model**

Replace the simple detail screen with the spec’s pane structure:

- `Sessions`
- `Generated Checkpoint Summary`
- `File Diff`
- `tab` focus cycling
- focused pane gets expanded rendering and scroll ownership
- unfocused panes render previews

Tests: pane focus, preview/expanded rendering, scroll ownership, `g`/`G`.

**PR 5: Session Detail Drilldown**

Add explicit session selection and session detail:

- session list supports movement and open
- session detail reuses/mirrors `entire explain --checkpoint` condensed transcript rendering
- initially keep it scrollable and readable before adding the more complex tool-call focus behavior

Tests: multi-session navigation, session content loading by index/ID, transcript fallback behavior.

**PR 6: Session Interaction Polish**

Add the richer session transcript behavior:

- tool-call-heavy stretches collapsed by default
- tool-call groups as bordered sections
- `tab` / `shift+tab` moves between tool-call groups
- `e` expands/collapses focused group
- viewport keeps focused group visible

Tests: group extraction/rendering, focus movement, expand/collapse, viewport positioning.

**PR 7: Highlighting And Diff Polish**

Add Chroma-backed rendering:

- syntax-highlight only the TUI code pane
- preserve metadata gutter styling through Lip Gloss
- improve diff rendering with add/remove colors and hunk preservation
- fallback cleanly when lexer detection fails

Note: Chroma is currently indirect in `go.mod`; importing it directly will make it a direct dependency, so I would treat this PR as the explicit dependency/polish PR.

**PR 8: No-Arg File Browser**

Add `entire why` interactive entry:

- browser rooted at current working directory, not repo root
- dotfiles included
- directories before files
- traversal via arrows, `j/k`, `enter`, `h`, backspace
- preserve browser directory/cursor when returning from file view
- non-interactive no-arg and forced `--interactive` without TTY fail clearly

Tests: sort order, path normalization to repo-relative Git path, state preservation, non-interactive failure.

I’d keep the command hidden through the whole prototype series, then do a tiny final “unhide or keep hidden” PR when the feature is ready for broader use.

settings.developer_instructions:
# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

The `request_user_input` tool is unavailable in Default mode. If you call it while in Default mode, it will return an error.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions. If you absolutely must ask a question because the answer cannot be discovered from local context and a reasonable assumption would be risky, ask the user directly with a concise plain-text question. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

payload.user_instructions:
## Workflow

### New features and non-trivial changes — Plan First

When building new functionality, refactoring, or making changes that span multiple files or affect architecture:

1. **Plan first:** Enter plan mode. Read relevant source files, trace execution paths, and write a step-by-step implementation plan. Exit plan mode and wait for approval before writing any code.
2. **Implement one step at a time:** After the plan is approved, implement ONE logical step (e.g., one new file, one function, one test group). Then STOP.
3. **Present changes for review:** After each step, show what changed (files modified, key decisions made) and wait for explicit approval before proceeding to the next step.

**"Yes" means "yes to the approach" — NOT "implement everything at once."** Approval of a plan or analysis is permission to start the first step, not to run through all steps uninterrupted. After completing each step, STOP and show what you did. Silence from me does not mean "keep going."

### Skill-driven workflows and small changes — Execute Directly

When following a skill (review, pr-feedback, simplify, pr, etc.) or making small targeted changes (fixing a lint issue, addressing a single review comment, tweaking a config):

- The skill defines the workflow. Follow it directly — do NOT layer plan mode on top.
- For small changes without a skill, read the relevant code, make the change, and present the result. No plan needed.

### Always

- **Never auto-commit:** NEVER create git commits unless the user explicitly asks. Present the completed work and let the user decide when to commit.
- When asked to explore or analyze code, ALWAYS read the actual source files. NEVER delegate to a Task agent or give surface-level answers without thorough codebase exploration.

## Search

When searching files, try to use faster tools like `ripgrep` rather than `grep`.

## Scope Control

NEVER modify files or code beyond what the task requires:
- No refactoring adjacent code, adding wrapper structs, or extracting abstractions unless explicitly requested
- No renaming, reorganizing, or "improving" code outside the task scope
- If you see improvement opportunities, list them separately at the end — NEVER bundle them into the change

When multiple items need attention (e.g., multiple failing agents, multiple commits), address ALL of them — not just the first one found. Confirm the full scope before starting work.

**Stop and ask before:** adding any dependency, changing function signatures in shared interfaces, or modifying code outside files directly related to the task.

## Go Development

After editing Go files, ALWAYS run `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, and `golangci-lint run ./...` before considering the task done. Fix any unused variables, compilation errors, or lint findings before presenting results.

Always ensure that the code will lint without any issues.

## Verification

When running linters, tests, or build commands, show the actual command output. NEVER summarize results as "passing" or "clean" without pasting the evidence. If a command fails, report the failure immediately — do not silently retry or omit it.

Before making claims about how the codebase works (what a struct contains, how a plugin behaves, whether a field exists), verify by reading the actual source. Do not guess based on naming conventions or prior context.

## Multi-Terminal Awareness

When I re-run a command (e.g., /simplify, /review) or ask you to look at something again, always re-read the current state from scratch — run fresh `git diff`, re-read files, etc. NEVER assume the code or branch state hasn't changed since the last time you checked. I frequently make changes from other terminals.

## Git Workflow

### Git Operations

When committing, ALWAYS combine `git add` and `git commit` into a single shell command (e.g., `git add file1.go file2.go && git commit -m "message"`). Do NOT run them as separate tool calls — that forces unnecessary approval prompts.

When reverting changes, use surgical git operations (e.g., `git checkout main -- <file>` or `git revert`) — NEVER hard-reset entire branches.

NEVER force push without my consent. Try to avoid amending commits. If there's a need for amending a commit, double check if the commit was already pushed to a remote. If it was, don't amend and create a new commit instead.

### Commit Messages

When writing commit messages, describe ONLY the net change between this commit and the previous one — the actual diff. NEVER describe:

- The process of arriving at the change (debugging steps, failed attempts, iterations)
- Conversations, decisions, or back-and-forth that happened during development
- Work that was done and then undone before committing
- Intermediate states that no longer exist in the final diff

The commit message must read as if a human wrote the code in one pass. A reader seeing only `git log` and `git diff` should find the message perfectly
sufficient — no hidden context needed.

Write the message by reading a diff (`git diff` or `git diff --cached`), not by recalling the session history. NEVER add `Co-Authored-By:` trailers. Write a semantically correct commit message only.

## "Commit and Continue" Protocol

When I say "commit and continue" (or any variation like "commit & continue", "commit, continue"):

1. **Commit** — Stage and commit ONLY the current uncommitted changes. Use a clear, semantically correct commit message. Do NOT amend previous commits. Do NOT push.
2. **Continue** — Immediately proceed to the next step in the current workflow (plan step, review finding, feedback item, etc.) and implement it. Do NOT stop to ask permission — "continue" means keep going.

"Commit and continue" is permission to implement the NEXT step, not to run through ALL remaining steps. After completing the next step, follow the normal workflow rules (e.g., stop after each plan step, stop after each supervised review finding).

## Pull Requests

Create complete but concise PR descriptions. Describe the problem solved and how it was implemented. Don't waste reviewer time. Do NOT add self-promotion to a pull request description. I don't want to see any "Generated with Claude Code" references in my pull requests ever.

## Plans

NEVER check in plan files unless explicitly asked. The `docs/plans` and `docs/superpowers` folders are git-ignored.

# Entire - CLI

This repo contains the CLI for Entire.

## Architecture

- CLI built with github.com/spf13/cobra and github.com/charmbracelet/huh

## Key Directories

### Commands (`cmd/`)

- `entire/`: Main CLI entry point
- `entire/cli`: CLI utilities and helpers
- `entire/cli/commands`: actual command implementations
- `entire/cli/agent`: agent implementations (Claude Code, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI) - see [Agent Integration Checklist](docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md) and [Agent Implementation Guide](docs/architecture/agent-guide.md)
- `entire/cli/strategy`: strategy implementation (manual-commit) - see section below
- `entire/cli/checkpoint`: checkpoint storage abstractions (temporary and committed)
- `entire/cli/session`: session state management
- `entire/cli/integration_test`: integration tests (simulated hooks)
- `e2e/`: E2E tests with real agent calls (see [e2e/README.md](e2e/README.md))

## Development

### Running Tests

```bash

```

### Running Integration Tests

```bash
mise run test:integration
```

### Running All Tests (CI)

```bash
mise run test:ci
```

This runs unit tests, integration tests, and the E2E canary (Vogon agent) in sequence. Integration tests use the `//go:build integration` build tag and are located in `cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/`.

### Running E2E Canary Tests (Vogon Agent)

The Vogon agent is a deterministic fake agent that exercises the full E2E test suite without making any API calls. Named after the Vogons from The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy — bureaucratic, procedural, and deterministic to a fault.

```bash
mise run test:e2e:canary           # Run all E2E tests with the Vogon agent
mise run test:e2e:canary TestFoo   # Run a specific test
```

- **Runs as part of `test:ci`** — canary failures block merges
- **No API calls, no cost** — safe to run freely, unlike real agent E2E tests
- **If a canary test fails, the bug is in the CLI or test infrastructure**, not in an agent
- Located in `e2e/vogon/` (binary) and `cmd/entire/cli/agent/vogon/` (Agent interface)
- The binary parses prompts via regex, creates/modifies/deletes files, and fires lifecycle hooks
- **IMPORTANT: When changing E2E test prompt wording**, the Vogon binary (`e2e/vogon/main.go`) parses prompts with hardcoded regexes. New phrasing may not match existing patterns — always run `mise run test:e2e:canary` after changing prompt text and fix Vogon's parsing if tests fail.

### Running E2E Tests (Only When Explicitly Requested)

**IMPORTANT: Do NOT run E2E tests proactively.** E2E tests make real API calls to agents, which consume tokens and cost money. Only run them when the user explicitly asks for E2E testing.

```bash
mise run test:e2e [filter]                          # All agents, filtered
mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code [filter]       # Claude Code only
mise run test:e2e --agent gemini-cli [filter]        # Gemini CLI only
mise run test:e2e --agent opencode [filter]          # OpenCode only

mise run test:e2e --agent factoryai-droid [filter]   # Factory AI Droid only
mise run test:e2e --agent copilot-cli [filter]       # Copilot CLI only
```

E2E tests:

- Located in `e2e/tests/`
- See [`e2e/README.md`](e2e/README.md) for full documentation (structure, debugging, adding agents)
